title: Stable Representation Learning on Graphs from Multiple Environments with Structure Distribution Shift

problem.claim: Graph Neural Networks may suffer serious performance impacts when selection bias affects node features and graph structures across environments.

gap.claim: Existing research has studied out-of-distribution problems involving feature distributions, but has paid little specific attention to bias in graph structure.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph Neural Networks are effective for utilizing graphs and have been applied in several real-world domains.
GNNs are generally trained and tested in environments with the same distribution.
Selection bias in node features and graph structures occurs in real cases and can substantially affect GNN performance.
Prior OOD research has focused mainly on feature distribution, leaving graph-structure bias less studied.
Graph structure is fundamental to GNNs because it strongly influences message propagation.

source_observation.claim: Graph structure can be a distinct source of distribution shift that affects GNN message propagation.

interpretation.claim: Robust graph learning should assess structural shift separately from feature shift.

application.claim: When deploying GNNs across environments, evaluate whether changes in graph connectivity or structure alter model behavior.

exception.claim: The supplied units do not establish that structural-shift evaluation is sufficient for all deployment settings.

unknowns: The proposed method or system is not described.
No experiments, datasets, metrics, numerical results, or comparisons are supplied.
The specific form of structural distribution shift is not defined.
